item.title: Reading a Zoo Map
item.description: Read a simple zoo map and visitor notices to find animals, plan a stop, and see which areas are closed.

children.definition: A very large animal with big ears and a long nose.
children.example: Look for the picture of an elephant to find where these animals live.

children.definition: A tall animal with a very long neck and brown spots.
children.example: The map shows a giraffe next to the north gate.

children.definition: An African animal like a horse with black and white lines on its body.
children.example: The picture of a zebra shows where you can see these black and white animals.

children.definition: An animal that can climb very well and usually has a long tail.
children.example: The notice says you may see a monkey high up in the trees.

children.definition: A black and white bird that can swim but cannot fly.
children.example: The picture of a penguin on the map shows where these birds swim.

children.definition: A large reptile with short legs, a long snout, and sharp teeth that lives in or near water.
children.example: The sign by the pool says a crocodile often lies under the heat lamp.

children.definition: A place with a fence or wall around it where zoo animals are kept.
children.example: Please stay outside the zebra enclosure.

children.definition: A zoo building where visitors can see animals such as snakes and lizards.
children.example: The map shows the reptile house beside the south gate.

children.definition: A place outside where people can sit and eat food they bring.
children.example: The map shows a picnic area with tables under the trees.

children.definition: A small picture or mark that shows what something is or where to find it.
children.example: The cup symbol on the zoo map shows where you can get a drink.

children.definition: A narrow way for people to walk on.
children.example: The dotted line on the zoo map shows a footpath through the trees.

children.definition: A short event where a zoo worker tells visitors about the animals they look after.
children.example: The notice says the keeper talk takes place beside the penguin pool.

children.definition: A device that sends a small stream of water up so people can drink from it directly.
children.example: The zoo map shows a drinking fountain next to the toilets.

children.definition: Used on a sign to show that only people who work there can go into a place.
children.example: The gate is marked “Staff Only,” so visitors must use the other gate.
